newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends firmer on expected dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends firmer on expected dollar inflows.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Wednesday on expectations of dollar inflows after the May 2 increase in the foreign shareholding limit, dealers said.
But forward dollar buying limited the won's rise.
The won closed at 891.90 against Tuesday's closing of 893.00. It traded in a tight range of 891.80 to 892.60.
Stock market analysts have forecast the expansion of the shareholding limit, to 23 percent from the current 20 percent, would bring in $500-$600 million.
The market will be closed on Thursday for the Labour Day.
Traders said month-end export negotiations were less than their earlier expectations.
They said many banks stayed sidelined before the foreign ownership expansion and the Labour Day holiday.

"The direction of the dollar would be determined by the intensity of the central bank's interventions on May 2," said one dealer, referring to expectations the Bank of Korea would heavily buy dollars to prevent the local currency's sharp rise.
Dealers saw the won's base mid-rate at 892.20 for Friday against 892.10 today.
